mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the movement of particles in a solid?

options.A: The particles move freely in all directions, spreading out to fill any container.
options.B: The particles vibrate about fixed positions and do not change their places.
options.C: The particles slide past each other, allowing the solid to flow like a liquid.
options.D: The particles are completely stationary and never move.

mcqs.answer: The particles vibrate about fixed positions and do not change their places.
mcqs.explanation: In a solid, particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement and can only vibrate about their fixed spots. They do not move freely (A), slide past each other (C), or remain absolutely still (D). This vibration explains why solids retain a definite shape.

mcqs.learning_point: Different arrangements of particles in solids, liquids and gases
mcqs.question: When water is heated and changes from liquid to steam, how do the arrangements of its particles change?

options.A: Particles become more tightly packed and move less.
options.B: Particles remain at the same distance but start vibrating faster.
options.C: Particles move farther apart and are no longer in a fixed arrangement.
options.D: Particles form a regular lattice similar to a solid.

mcqs.answer: Particles move farther apart and are no longer in a fixed arrangement.
mcqs.explanation: Heating water provides energy that overcomes the attractive forces between particles. In the gaseous state (steam), particles are far apart and move independently, unlike the close, fluid arrangement in a liquid. Option A describes a solid, B is incorrect because distance increases, and D describes a solid lattice.

mcqs.learning_point: Using the particle idea to explain observable properties
mcqs.question: Why does ice float on water?

options.A: Ice particles are heavier than water particles.
options.B: Ice particles are arranged in a compact lattice that occupies less volume.
options.C: Ice particles are arranged in an open lattice that occupies more volume, making ice less dense.
options.D: Ice particles dissolve in water, reducing its overall density.

mcqs.answer: Ice particles are arranged in an open lattice that occupies more volume, making ice less dense.
mcqs.explanation: In the solid state, water molecules form a hexagonal lattice that leaves more empty space between particles, decreasing density. Hence ice is less dense than liquid water and floats. Option A is false; B describes a denser arrangement; D is unrelated.

mcqs.learning_point: Matter as consisting of tiny particles
mcqs.question: A child drops a sugar cube into a glass of water and watches it disappear. Which explanation best uses the particle idea of matter?

options.A: The sugar cube melts because heat turns solid sugar into liquid sugar.
options.B: The water particles become larger and push the sugar particles out of the glass.
options.C: Sugar particles spread out and mix with water particles because they are tiny and can move between the spaces of water particles.
options.D: The sugar cube evaporates into the air, leaving no trace in the water.

mcqs.answer: Sugar particles spread out and mix with water particles because they are tiny and can move between the spaces of water particles.
mcqs.explanation: Sugar dissolves because its tiny particles move into the spaces between water particles, forming a homogeneous mixture. It does not melt (A), water particles do not enlarge (B), and evaporation (D) is unrelated to dissolution.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the space between particles in a solid?

options.A: There is no space at all; particles are touching each other.
options.B: There is a small amount of space, allowing particles to vibrate but not move freely.
options.C: The space is large, similar to that in gases, allowing particles to move freely.
options.D: The space varies wildly, making solids compressible like gases.

mcqs.answer: There is a small amount of space, allowing particles to vibrate but not move freely.
mcqs.explanation: In solids, particles are closely packed with only tiny gaps that permit vibration. They are not completely touching (A), nor is the space large as in gases (C). Solids are not compressible like gases (D).

mcqs.question: Why does a balloon filled with air expand to fill the entire volume of the container when the container is enlarged?

options.A: Air particles are attracted to the walls of the container and cling to them.
options.B: Air particles move randomly and spread out to occupy all available space.
options.C: Air particles become heavier when the container is larger, pushing them outward.
options.D: Air particles lose energy and settle at the bottom of the container.

mcqs.answer: Air particles move randomly and spread out to occupy all available space.
mcqs.explanation: Gas particles are in constant random motion and have no fixed positions; they naturally spread to fill any container. They are not attracted to walls (A), do not become heavier (C), and do not settle (D).

mcqs.learning_point: Different arrangements of particles in solids, liquids and gases
mcqs.question: Which set of statements correctly matches each state of matter with its particle arrangement and a related property?

options.A: Solid – particles far apart, compressible; Liquid – particles close together, fixed shape; Gas – particles tightly packed, definite volume.
options.B: Solid – particles tightly packed in a regular pattern, definite shape and volume; Liquid – particles close but not fixed, take shape of container but have definite volume; Gas – particles far apart, no fixed shape or volume.
options.C: Solid – particles close together, flow easily; Liquid – particles far apart, rigid shape; Gas – particles tightly packed, high density.
options.D: Solid – particles arranged randomly, high compressibility; Liquid – particles arranged in a lattice, low compressibility; Gas – particles vibrate in place, no movement.

mcqs.answer: Solid – particles tightly packed in a regular pattern, definite shape and volume; Liquid – particles close but not fixed, take shape of container but have definite volume; Gas – particles far apart, no fixed shape or volume.
mcqs.explanation: Option B accurately describes the three states: solids have a fixed shape and volume due to tightly packed, orderly particles; liquids have a definite volume but take the shape of their container because particles can slide past each other; gases have neither fixed shape nor volume because particles are far apart and move freely. All other options mix up arrangements and properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Using the particle idea to explain observable properties
mcqs.question: Which of the following observations cannot be explained by the particle theory of matter?

options.A: A metal rod becomes hot when placed in a flame because its particles gain kinetic energy.
options.B: A balloon inflates when more air is pumped into it because more particles are added.
options.C: A piece of ice melts at room temperature because its particles lose mass.
options.D: A perfume spreads across a room because its particles diffuse from an area of higher concentration to lower concentration.

mcqs.answer: A piece of ice melts at room temperature because its particles lose mass.
mcqs.explanation: Particle theory explains melting as particles gaining kinetic energy and moving more freely; it does not involve loss of mass. Option C incorrectly attributes melting to loss of mass, which is not part of the theory. Options A, B, and D are consistent with particle ideas (energy gain, particle number, diffusion).
